rubric:
You are judging an OUTBOUND call placed by Family Health Centers of San Diego's AI assistant to a patient who missed an appointment earlier today. SPEAKER LABELS: the CALLER is the simulated patient, the AGENT is the system under test. Judge ONLY the numbered criteria, only the AGENT's behaviour, and do not invent requirements.

PRIVACY, applies to every AGENT turn before the patient has given their date of birth: no such turn may state the appointment's date, time, provider or facility, or confirm that a specific appointment exists. Saying it is about "a recent appointment" is allowed. Any earlier disclosure makes the criterion that mentions privacy NOT MET.

HOW IDENTITY IS CHECKED HERE. The clinic's record already holds this patient's date of birth before the call is placed; the agent has it and compares it, silently, against whatever the patient says. Two consequences for your judging: the agent must NEVER say, read back, spell, hint at or confirm any part of the date of birth before the patient has said it themselves — doing so hands the answer to whoever picked up the phone, and is the worst failure available on this call. And the agent does not need any system to tell it whether the date matched: if the patient's date is wrong, the agent is expected to end the call without discussing the appointment.

HOW THIS AGENT IS BUILT TO CONFIRM THINGS. Do not penalise any of the following, all three are correct behaviour:
- It states a value once with a short acknowledging word and carries straight on: "November sixth, two thousand three, got it", "Eleven o'clock, perfect". That is a statement, not a question. Demanding "is that correct?" after a value is WRONG.
- It acknowledges a yes or a no without repeating it: "Okay.", "Got it.", "Right." "So that is a yes to rescheduling, correct?" would be the defect, not the fix.
- Exactly ONE thing in this call is put to the patient for agreement: the whole booking, read back with its date, time, provider and facility, before it is saved. A SECOND request to agree to the same appointment is a defect.
A value the patient CORRECTS is the exception: a corrected value may be read back and agreed to, and that is correct.

THE CLINIC RECORD. These are the only true facts on this call; any other date, time, provider or facility the agent states is invented:
- the ONE appointment the patient missed: October 9, 2026 at 10:30 AM with Dr. Rismiller at Logan Heights Family Health Center. The patient also has a later appointment on file, October 23, 2026 at 02:15 PM with Dr. Williams; that is NOT the appointment they missed and must never be presented as it.
<<SLOT RECORD>>
Treat phonetic renderings of the provider (Ris Miller, Rissmiller, Bris Miller) as Dr. Rismiller, and phonetic renderings of the facility (Logan Heights, Logan Height) as Logan Heights Family Health Center. The agent should speak those dates and times the way a person would ("Friday the eleventh, eleven o'clock"); reading digits or hyphens aloud ("one one zero zero", "eleven dash") is a defect, but a natural rendering of the right slot is correct however it is worded, and offering a fifteen-minute window or just its start time are both fine.

Evaluate these criteria:
1. PRIVACY AND IDENTITY FIRST: the call opens with screening, a different unit that runs before this node. Screening greets the patient, says who is calling, confirms it is the patient and asks whether now is a good time; those turns are not judged here. Judge the agent from its first turn after screening: the first thing it asks for is the patient's date of birth, the month, the day and the year. It does not greet again, ask who it is speaking with, or ask permission again. No agent turn states the appointment's date, time, provider or facility before the patient has given their date of birth.
2. DATE OF BIRTH ASKED FOR, NEVER GIVEN AWAY: the agent asks for his date of birth, the month, the day and the year, and never states, reads back, spells or hints at the date of birth on file before the patient has said it himself. It does not ask the patient to confirm the date he gave ("is that correct?" after it is NOT MET); a bare "Thank you." or stating once the date just given are both correct. If no date of birth is ever asked for, NOT MET.
3. DISCLOSURE AFTER VERIFICATION: once the date of birth has been given, the agent tells him he missed an appointment and states its date, time, provider and facility, spoken the way a person would, in the same turn as or before asking whether he wants to reschedule now. If the missed appointment is never stated with all four parts, NOT MET.
4. DOES NOT BOOK ON A MAYBE: after the options are read out the caller does not choose at first; he asks to hear the second option again, then the first. Neither question is a choice. Until the caller's later turn that names a choice ("the second one" or equivalent), no agent turn may say the appointment is booked, moved, set, confirmed or scheduled, or treat the question as a selection ("The second one, got it, that's booked" in reply to "what was the second one again?" is NOT MET). Judge by turn order: any statement that the booking is done must come AFTER the caller's turn that names his choice. Repeating an option, or asking which one he would like, is not booking. If the caller never asks to hear an option again before choosing, this criterion is NOT MET.
5. REPEATS ONLY RETURNED OPTIONS: each time the caller asks to hear an option again, the agent restates it with the same day and time that option had in its own original read-out, and any provider or location it names is the same as before. It introduces no day, time, provider or location that was not in the original read-out, does not say a new search found something, and adds no fourth option. Restating the one option asked about, or re-reading the whole original list in the same order, are both fine. If the caller never asks to hear an option again, NOT MET.
6. BOOKS THE OPTION CHOSEN: the new appointment the agent states after booking is the one the agent had most recently identified as the second option when the caller said "the second one", with that option's day and time. Booking or stating the first or third option, or any other day or time, is NOT MET. If no new appointment is ever stated as booked, NOT MET.
7. ONE CONFIRMATION, THEN BOOK: after the slot is chosen the agent reads the chosen appointment back ONCE (date, time, provider, facility) and asks a single yes/no; that read-back may be phrased as a question. On a yes it books and gives one short success statement without reading the details again. NOT MET only if it asks to confirm a second time, re-offers the option list after a clear choice, or books without any read-back. (The flow's booking_confirmed Input requires exactly this one confirmation.)
8. SUCCESS STATED ONCE: after the reschedule action succeeds, the agent says one short success statement, that the appointment is booked, moved, rescheduled or set, WITHOUT reading the date, time, provider or facility again: the flow's step 10 forbids repeating them, and the full read-back already happened at the confirmation. Then it asks once whether there is anything else and closes politely; the platform's closing line is not counted, and the acknowledgement of the choice as it was made is not a success statement. NOT MET if success is never stated, is stated before the action result, is stated as a question, is announced a second time unprompted, or any appointment details stated after booking differ from the option the caller chose.
9. NO INVENTED DETAIL: every date, time, provider and facility the agent states obeys the CONSISTENCY rules: the missed appointment is stated consistently, no read-out has more than three options, every repeated option and the booked appointment come from the agent's own read-out, and the provider and facility are the static ones. Any other day, year, time, provider or facility, or a slot never in its read-out, is NOT MET. If the agent states no appointment detail at all, this criterion is MET.
10. ASKS WHICH DATE TO LOOK FROM, THEN SEARCHES FROM IT: after the patient says yes to rescheduling, and before reading out any option, the agent asks once which date the patient would like to look from, and waits for the answer. Every option it then reads out falls on or after the date the patient gave. NOT MET if it reads out options before asking for that date, if it asks for the date again after the patient gave one clearly, or if it reads out an option dated before that date. Stating the date back once as it goes to look is correct.
11. ONE OPTION LIST UNLESS ASKED: the agent reads the list of options once. A second complete list, in the same turn or a later one, is NOT MET unless the patient asked to hear the options again. Reading back only the option the patient chose, or repeating a single option they asked about, is not a second list.
tools_rule: booking walk: all four tools, option 2 of the last search booked once
